title: Explainable AI
targetDuration: 1–2 minutes; hard maximum 120 seconds after measured voice timing

scenes.title: The explanation looks convincing
scenes.viewerPurpose: The explanation has failed a person’s practical need. The book separates persuasive accounts from support.
scenes.composition: A person receives a rejection while a colorful model explanation fails to answer their question. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: A person receives a rejection while a colorful model explanation fails to answer their question.
Place the displayed explanation beside a record of how the decision was actually made.

cues.text: A model rejects someone, and the colorful explanation still cannot tell them why it happened.
cues.visualAction: A person receives a rejection while a colorful model explanation fails to answer their question.
cues.emotion: Quiet concern; gently emphasize “cannot tell them why”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: Explainable AI asks how to tell a persuasive account of a decision from evidence about how it was made.
cues.visualAction: Place the displayed explanation beside a record of how the decision was actually made.
cues.emotion: Clear curiosity; gently emphasize “evidence”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

scenes.title: What question did it answer?
scenes.viewerPurpose: The purpose depends on who needs an answer. Several tasks need different kinds of help.
scenes.composition: Show the person’s specific question before introducing any method labels. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: Show the person’s specific question before introducing any method labels.
Keep debugging, appeal and deployment questions as separate destinations from the same system.

cues.text: It starts with a practical question: what does this person need the explanation to answer?
cues.visualAction: Show the person’s specific question before introducing any method labels.
cues.emotion: Patient care; gently emphasize “this person”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: Fixing a system, challenging a decision, and deciding whether to use it can require different explanations.
cues.visualAction: Keep debugging, appeal and deployment questions as separate destinations from the same system.
cues.emotion: Plain distinction; gently emphasize “different explanations”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

scenes.title: A highlighted region proves what?
scenes.viewerPurpose: The methods are introduced without jargon. An explanation is not automatically a usable way forward.
scenes.composition: Highlight one input while its comparison baseline remains visible. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: Highlight one input while its comparison baseline remains visible.
Let the highlighted detail stop short of a feasible route around the person’s actual obstacle.

cues.text: The book compares ways of highlighting inputs, testing possible changes, and examining the model’s inner workings.
cues.visualAction: Highlight one input while its comparison baseline remains visible.
cues.emotion: Accessible interest; gently emphasize “testing possible changes”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: A highlighted detail may still leave the person wondering what they could realistically do differently.
cues.visualAction: Let the highlighted detail stop short of a feasible route around the person’s actual obstacle.
cues.emotion: Human concern; gently emphasize “realistically do differently”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

scenes.title: A change someone can make
scenes.viewerPurpose: The reader has a clear inspection task. The unresolved complaint is a concrete opening.
scenes.composition: A reviewer examines the explanation alongside the original decision. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: A reviewer examines the explanation alongside the original decision.
End with the person and an open practical question, rather than a completed correction.

cues.text: Builders and users are invited to question an explanation as carefully as the decision it explains.
cues.visualAction: A reviewer examines the explanation alongside the original decision.
cues.emotion: Practical invitation; gently emphasize “as carefully”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: Begin with the rejected person, whose question the colorful dashboard has not yet answered.
cues.visualAction: End with the person and an open practical question, rather than a completed correction.
cues.emotion: Soft emphasis; gently emphasize “has not yet answered”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.
